clue.text: Presumably, dark glasses are ideal protection from it?

definitions.text: Presumably, dark glasses are ideal protection from it?

parts.words: Presumably, dark glasses are ideal protection from it
parts.note: dark glasses suggest night, and the joke is a sun that shines at night, as in polar summers

explanation.surface: Someone recommends sunglasses as the perfect shield against some glare.
explanation.walkthrough: The paradox is the point: glasses as dark as midnight would suit a sun that shines at midnight, seen in Arctic and Antarctic summers.
explanation.definitionFit: In polar summer the sun stays above the horizon all night, a phenomenon named for the hour.

clue.text: In which goods are paid for in notes?

definitions.text: In which goods are paid for in notes?

parts.words: In which goods are paid for in notes
parts.note: notes sounds like banknotes, but it means letters asking for goods sent by post

explanation.surface: A trading system where people pay cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notes' suggests cash; the buying is done by written request sent through the post.
explanation.definitionFit: Catalogue shopping by post, where goods are requested by letter and delivered by mail.

clue.text: Abandoned aircraft brought down in sea

definitions.meaning: said of a plane forced to land on water

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both dumped or discarded, and of a plane, forced down onto water.

clue.text: Pressing an item brought from overseas on worker

parts.note: goods brought in from abroad are imports
a worker ant is the usual crossword worker

explanation.surface: Someone is ironing a foreign-made item on top of a labourer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pressing' reads like ironing in the surface, but it is the definition, meaning urgent; 'on' is the charade signal and 'an' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A pressing matter is urgent and significant, demanding attention now.

clue.text: Lift is about to be stolen…

indicators.note: about means the word for stolen goes round the other piece

parts.note: stolen goods are hot
taken as written

explanation.surface: An elevator is going to be taken by thieves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals the container. 'Lift' tempts as a synonym of steal beside 'stolen', but here it means raise.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise a heavy load with tackle or by hand is the same act as lifting it.

clue.text: … to purloin a bit of horse

definitions.meaning: a jointed mouthpiece fitted on a bridle

explanation.definitionFit: The word is British slang for pinching something, and also a simple jointed bit used in a horse's mouth.

clue.text: A row of engines at full blast, perhaps!

definitions.text: A row of engines at full blast, perhaps!

parts.words: A row of engines at full blast, perhaps
parts.note: a row sounds like a line of machines, but means a din, the racket they make running flat out

explanation.surface: A line of motors running flat out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' rhymes here with cow, not toe: a racket, not a line.
explanation.definitionFit: A row is a din, the loud sound engines make running flat out.

clue.text: Bricked up, maybe?

parts.note: bricked up sounds like sealing a doorway, but read as constructed from bricks it describes any brick building put up

explanation.surface: A doorway or window has perhaps been sealed with masonry.
explanation.definitionFit: A wall that has been bricked up has been constructed, raised from bricks by a builder.

clue.text: Drab cabinet reshuffle what a bore

indicators.note: a cabinet reshuffle rearranges ministers, so these letters are rearranged too

explanation.surface: A dull reshuffle of government ministers is tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reshuffle' rearranges DRABCABINET; 'bore' seems to mean tedium but is a tool that bores holes.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand drill made of a cranked handle and a drilling bit, used to bore holes in wood.

clue.text: Starchy old goat assisting hopeful candidate in the US

definitions.text: assisting hopeful candidate in the US

parts.note: starchy means stiffly formal, prim
Aries is the zodiac's horned ram, here loosely a horned old billy

explanation.surface: A stuffy, lecherous old man is helping someone running for office in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old goat' is a stretch for the zodiac Ram, Aries, but it is the only piece that completes the letters after PRIM.
explanation.definitionFit: American primaries are preliminary party elections that help a hopeful become the party's nominee.

clue.text: National confidence?

parts.note: confidence suggests self-belief, but here it means something told in confidence, kept by a nation

explanation.surface: A country's self-belief.
explanation.definitionFit: Information a government keeps classified is a secret held by the nation.

clue.text: No earth shattering description of someone else

indicators.note: shattering breaks the two words into pieces to be rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: An announcement that is not earth-shattering at all describes some other person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shattering' rearranges NOEARTH into the answer; the surface wants the phrase 'no earth-shattering'.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone a different person, not this one, is the very word used to describe them.

clue.text: Material Welsh runner put on Basques

parts.note: a river is a runner, and the Taff is the river flowing through Cardiff in Wales
ETA was the armed Basque separatist group

explanation.surface: A Welsh athlete has pulled on some fitted bodices for a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on' is the charade signal; 'Basques' suggests corsets, but means the people, via their separatist group.
explanation.definitionFit: Taffeta is a crisp woven silk or synthetic fabric used for gowns.

clue.text: Finished up in padded negligee!

indicators.note: in a down-going sense, up means the run of letters is read from the bottom, backwards
in shows the letters sit within the words padded negligee

explanation.surface: Someone finished up wearing a quilted nightgown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' takes DEDNE from padDED NEgligee and 'up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that has ended is over, completed, brought to a close.

clue.text: One entitled to get the post of director

definitions.text: One entitled to get the post of director

parts.words: One entitled to get the post of director
parts.note: sounds like someone with a right to a top job, but means the person whose name and direction is on the letters delivered

explanation.surface: A person has a right to be appointed director.
explanation.walkthrough: 'post' means mail, not a job, and 'director' hints at the directions, the old word for an envelope's written address.
explanation.definitionFit: The person a letter is directed to receives the mail bearing their name.

clue.text: Mount of jet with unknown value

parts.note: jet is a deep black, so dark
a mount is a horse to ride

explanation.surface: A jet-black horse whose worth nobody knows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' sets jet before the mount; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A contestant whose ability is a mystery may surprise everyone by winning.

clue.text: Miss England brought her career to an end in France

definitions.text: Miss England brought her career to an end in France

parts.words: Miss England brought her career to an end in France
parts.note: Miss England sounds like a beauty queen, but means a young woman whom the English burned at Rouen

explanation.surface: A beauty queen retired while in France.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Miss' as a young woman, not a pageant title: the English had Joan of Arc burned at Rouen in 1431.
explanation.definitionFit: Joan of Arc, the French maid executed by the English, was later canonised.

clue.text: Lighter captains use it for navigation

definitions.text: Lighter captains use it for navigation

parts.words: Lighter captains use it for navigation
parts.note: a lighter is a flat barge, so its skippers steer by a fixed point in the night sky

explanation.surface: People who carry less weight in charge apparently steer by some guide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lighter' looks like a comparative adjective but is a noun: a barge used to unload ships.
explanation.definitionFit: Polaris stays almost fixed above the pole, so sailors have long steered by it.

clue.text: In the lobby, find aged bag

indicators.note: In puts the word for aged inside the word for lobby

parts.note: a lobby or entrance is a hall
aged means old

explanation.surface: Someone finds an old bag in the hotel foyer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' signals the container; 'find' is a link. 'aged bag' tempts as an insult, but 'bag' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A large soft travelling bag that takes everything you pack.

clue.text: Shoot at a bird

definitions.meaning: to fire at someone from hiding
a long-billed wading bird of marshes

explanation.definitionFit: To fire from cover is the verb; the long-billed marsh wader is the bird of the same name.

clue.text: Chooses the best places to drink in up North!

definitions.text: the best places to drink in up North
definitions.meaning: in northern English pubs the select is the better-furnished best room

explanation.walkthrough: 'up North' means the north of England, where a pub's best room was traditionally the select.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means picks; northern English pubs called their smart lounge bar the select room.

clue.text: Gave the air of being boiled?

definitions.text: Gave the air of being boiled?

parts.words: Gave the air of being boiled
parts.note: gave the air sounds like seeming, but here air literally forms pockets as liquid boils

explanation.surface: Someone looked as though they had been cooked in water.
explanation.definitionFit: A boiling liquid throws up pockets of air and vapour, gurgling and seething as it heats.

clue.text: Bellyaches caused by meat? Up to a point

definitions.text: Bellyaches caused by meat? Up to a point

parts.words: Bellyaches caused by meat? Up to a point
parts.note: bellyaches are complaints, and partly they come from meat, since the word also names cattle meat

explanation.surface: Stomach upsets come from eating meat, sometimes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bellyaches' means grumbles, not stomach pains; the word is only half about meat, hence 'up to a point'.
explanation.definitionFit: Grumbles or complaints are slang beefs, and the word also names cuts of cattle meat.

clue.text: Joe Miller's in need of a clean-up!

definitions.meaning: a Joe Miller is a stale old joke, after an 18th-century jestbook, so Joe Miller is means stale
covered in grime that wants wiping

explanation.walkthrough: 'Joe Miller's' reads 'Joe Miller is': a Joe Miller is a hackneyed joke, from the 1739 collection Joe Miller's Jests.
explanation.definitionFit: Stale and old like a worn-out joke, and literally covered in grime needing a wipe.

clue.text: Used when the order is shoulder arms?

definitions.text: Used when the order is shoulder arms?

parts.words: Used when the order is shoulder arms
parts.note: the drill command shoulder arms is read as a pistol worn at the shoulder

explanation.surface: A parade-ground command calls for some piece of kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shoulder arms' is a rifle drill order; read literally it means carrying a gun at the shoulder, in a shoulder case.
explanation.definitionFit: A case for a pistol may be strapped under the shoulder, carrying the firearm ready to draw.

clue.text: King Mark supplied his country's finances

definitions.text: King Mark supplied his country's finances

parts.words: King Mark supplied his country's finances
parts.note: King Mark looks like the Cornish king of legend, but means a German ruler whose currency was the mark

explanation.surface: A legendary king funded his realm.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests King Mark of Cornwall from the Tristan legend; really the mark was German money, and the German emperor was the ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: The German emperor's title derives from Caesar, and Germany's currency under him was the mark.

clue.text: It means having power to hit

definitions.meaning: influence or pull, as in political weight

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both influence held over others and a heavy blow struck with the hand.

clue.text: Nutty Slack Month wittily covered by the press?

definitions.text: Nutty Slack Month wittily covered by the press?

parts.words: Nutty Slack Month wittily covered by the press
parts.note: nutty slack is a grade of small coal, but here nutty means daft and slack month a quiet time for news

explanation.surface: Newspapers are making jokes about a month dedicated to coal dust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nutty slack' is a British name for small coal; split it as nutty plus slack month, the summer lull when papers print trivial stories.
explanation.definitionFit: Summer, when Parliament is in recess and news is thin, papers fill pages with frivolous stories.
